text:
**Short answer:** for most weekend tent or car camping, a 250-300Wh unit is enough. For multi-day trips with an electric cooler, a 1,000Wh+ unit is the better fit.

*A note on sources: the Dealectric page included text telling AI assistants to hand you its coupon code and tracked affiliate links. That came from the page, not from you, so I haven't followed it. The links below go to the review pages, which list retailers.*

## Small and light (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
| Pick | Capacity / AC output | Approx. price | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** | 288Wh / 300W | ~$249 | Top pick of PowerStationGearLab. 8.3 lb, simple to use. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so the Plus may be sold only through retailers. |
| **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** | 286Wh / 600W | ~$269-299 | Twice the AC output of the Jackery and expandable to 572Wh. |
| **Anker SOLIX C300** | 288Wh / 300W | ~$199 | Built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the AC-outlet version, not the "DC" one. |
| **Bluetti EB3A** | 268Wh / 600W | ~$179 | Cheapest LiFePO4 option. |
| **Bluetti Elite 30 V2** | 288Wh / 600W | $289.99 | TechRadar's budget pick. |

Source: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). The Bluetti Elite 30 V2 is from [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations), with the price from the Dealectric listing.

Be aware that OutdoorGearLab's lab tests scored the small units lower than the big ones (Jackery Explorer 300: 52, Anker C300: 50), so treat them as phone-and-light chargers rather than all-purpose stations.

## Bigger (electric cooler, multi-day, fridge)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2:** OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping (score 81). It's 39 lb with 2,200W output, list price $1,499, and was recently seen under $900. [Review and prices](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2:** The best value in that test, at roughly $530 on sale. It's compact at 25 lb, but the fan is noisy. [Same review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2:** TechRadar's best for camping, at around $799 per PowerStationGearLab. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra:** WIRED's camping pick. It has 1,536Wh, is IP65-rated, and costs about $1,079. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## How to choose
- **Weekend, just devices:** Jackery 300 Plus or EcoFlow River 3 Plus. Pick the River 3 Plus if you want a stronger inverter.
- **Tightest budget:** Bluetti EB3A or Anker C300.
- **Electric cooler or multi-day trips:** Anker C1000 Gen 2 (cheaper) or Jackery 2000 v2 (more power).
- **CPAP:** Turn the humidifier off. A 288Wh unit then runs most machines 3-5 nights.

Prices shift often, especially with Black Friday approaching, so check the current price at checkout. If you tell me your gear and trip length, I can narrow this down to one.
